response:
Pointwise convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.

Consider the sequence of polynomials B_n(x) = x^n. This sequence converges pointwise to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1), but not uniformly. In fact, the sequence converges uniformly to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1) but not on [0, 1].

To see this, note that for any fixed x in [0, 1), the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges to 0 as n approaches infinity. However, the sequence does not converge uniformly on [0, 1) because for any fixed n, the set {x ∈ [0, 1) : x^n ≥ 1/n} has positive measure. This set is unbounded as n approaches infinity, which implies that the sequence B_n(x) does not converge uniformly on [0, 1).

In contrast, the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges uniformly to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1) because for any ε > 0, there exists N such that for all n > N, |x^n - 0| < ε for all x in [0, 1). This is because x^n ≤ 1 for all x in [0, 1).

Therefore, pointwise convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.
